name: excess_at_most_two_at_d_one
statement: For every LINEAR triangle system and every one-dimensional R = span{v}, the dual D collapses by at most 2, and the value 2 is attained exactly when v = e_x + e_y for a pair {x,y} lying in a triangle. Hence excess <= 2d holds at d = 1, and the excess-2 directions are exactly the 3k pair-sums, three per triangle.
notes: PROOF BY CASES, using D = {e_j} union {f_t} and the fact that a merge is a pair f -/+ g in span{v}. (a) v = e_x + e_y with {x,y} inside a triangle t = {a,x,y}: two merges exist, e_x - (-e_y) = v and f_t - e_a = v. There is no third - another coordinate pair would need e_i -/+ e_j = e_x+e_y forcing {i,j} = {x,y}; another triangle merge would need f_s - e_j = e_x+e_y, i.e. s = {j,x,y} contains {x,y}, so s = t BECAUSE LINEARITY PERMITS AT MOST ONE TRIANGLE ON A GIVEN PAIR; and f_s -/+ f_u = v is impossible since for a linear system |s int u| <= 1, so f_s - f_u has support >= 4 and f_s + f_u has support >= 5. Exactly 2. (b) v = e_x - e_y: the coordinate merge exists; a second would need f_t - f_s = e_x - e_y, support 2, requiring |t int s| = 2, forbidden; f_t -/+ e_j = e_x - e_y is impossible since f_t has all coefficients +1. Exactly 1. (c) v of support >= 3: no coordinate pair reaches it; two triangle-coordinate merges coinciding would give f_t - f_s = e_j -/+ e_i of support 2, again forcing |t int s| = 2; and f_t - f_s with |t int s| = 1 has sign pattern (+,+,-,-) while f_u - e_i has (+,+,+,-), so they cannot coincide. At most 1. || THIS ALSO PROVES WHY LINEARITY IS THE HYPOTHESIS: every step that could fail does so through one door, f_t - f_s dropping to support 2, which happens exactly when two triangles share an EDGE. That is the book p=3 witness in general form. || It upgrades pairsum_characterization_of_excess_two from measured to proved at d = 1. It does NOT close the composition: a subspace is not the union of its lines, and excess <= 2d is now known FALSE at d = 3 (see excess_at_most_2d_refuted). This d = 1 statement survives that refutation untouched and is the c = 0, E = d = 1 case of excess = 2d + c.

name: E_c_at_most_d
statement: Write excess = E_c + E_t, splitting the collapse of D by what each merge consumes: E_c counts coordinate merges e_i ~ e_j and E_t counts merges consuming a triangle form f_t. Then E_c <= d for every subspace R of dimension d. Proof: a coordinate merge requires e_i -/+ e_j in R, and E_c equals the number of edges of a spanning forest of the coordinate-merge graph, whose signed incidence vectors are linearly independent and all lie in R; so E_c <= dim R = d.
notes: This is the surviving half of the excess <= 2d derivation. Its partner E_t <= d was the one unproved link for the whole day and is now REFUTED (see E_t_at_most_d_refuted). Recorded separately from excess_at_most_two_per_dimension precisely because the composite bound fell and this half did not. || TIGHT ON ALL THREE COUNTEREXAMPLE WITNESSES, by direct recomputation while filing this store: E_c = 3 at d = 3 (tri-cycle k=4), E_c = 5 at d = 5 (tri-cycle k=6), E_c = 6 at d = 6 (two tri-cycle k=4 blocks). So the excess overshoot in each is carried entirely by E_t.

name: excess_equals_two_d_plus_cycle_rank
statement: Let R be spanned by merge-carrying pair-sum lines. Write E for the number of such lines lying in R and c for the cycle rank of the graph they form on the coordinates. Unsigned incidence gives d = E - c; each line carries two merges; each independent cycle costs exactly one coincidence. Hence excess = 2E - c = 2d + c. The refuted bounds excess <= 2d and excess <= 2d+1 are the c = 0 and c = 1 cases, and there is no reason for c to stop at 1.
notes: MATCHES BOTH COUNTEREXAMPLES EXACTLY: one tri-cycle k=4 block gives 2*3 + 1 = 7; two disjoint such blocks give 2*6 + 2 = 14. The second was predicted from additivity BEFORE it was run. || STATUS is heuristic and the label is deliberate: the derivation is a counting sketch about R spanned by pair-sum lines, not a theorem about arbitrary R, and it is fitted to two data points plus a mechanism. What it is good for is a shape, not a value. || WHAT IT THREATENS: since 2d + c = d + E, the counting requirement excess >= k becomes d + E >= k, and a configuration with many pair-sum lines on few coordinates makes E large while d stays small. See how_far_dense_linear_systems_erode_the_counting_bound.

name: tri_cycle_excess_seven_at_d_three
statement: Tri-cycle k=4 (triangles (0,1,2),(2,3,4),(4,5,6),(6,7,0); r = 8, |D| = 12) with R = span{e0+e2, e2+e4, e4+e6}: dim R = 3, classes come out [4,2,2,2,2], so excess = 7 > 2d = 6. Tri-cycle k=6 with R = span{e0+e2, e2+e4, e4+e6, e6+e8, e8+e10}: dim 5, excess 11 > 10. Controls in the same pass: one pair-sum gives excess 2 at d = 1, two disjoint pair-sums give 4 at d = 2.
notes: THE MECHANISM: four pair-sums forming a cycle in the coordinate graph are linearly dependent - (e0+e2) - (e2+e4) + (e4+e6) = e0+e6, which is the fourth pair-sum - so a 3-dimensional R can contain FOUR merge-carrying pair-sum lines, each carrying its two merges with one coincidence. || THESE ARE LINEAR SYSTEMS. Consecutive triangles in a tri-cycle share exactly one coordinate, so this is not the non-linear escape hatch of the book/wheel/fan family. Linearity is NOT sufficient for excess <= 2d; excess <= 2d is a TREE phenomenon (a tree has no coordinate cycle among its pair-sums, so the construction cannot be run there, which is why the exhaustive tree sweeps at d <= 3 saw max excess exactly 2d and no violation). || It was constructed deliberately from the trade-off identified when the per-line composition route was closed off, i.e. it was hunted rather than stumbled on. || INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED while filing this store, on a reimplementation of the merge/class machinery written from the definitions alone: |D| = 12, d = 3, five classes, sizes [4,2,2,2,2], excess 7 - every reported figure including the class-size vector - and the k=6 witness likewise at |D| = 18, d = 5, seven classes, excess 11. Both controls reproduce too (one pair-sum excess 2 at d = 1, two disjoint pair-sums excess 4 at d = 2), so the reproduction is not a dead detector.

name: two_block_tri_cycle_excess_fourteen_at_d_six
statement: Two coordinate-disjoint copies of tri-cycle k=4 (k = 8, r = 16, |D| = 24), taking the same three pair-sums from each block: dim R = 6 and excess = 14, against 2d = 12 and 2d+1 = 13.
notes: STATED IN ADVANCE and additive: d_cb and the class structure add over coordinate-disjoint blocks, so two copies of an excess-7 configuration at dim 3 must give excess 14 at dim 6. The prediction was registered before the run and the run confirmed it, so this is a designed falsification of excess <= 2d+1 rather than a search result. || INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED while filing this store: |D| = 24, d = 6, ten classes, excess 14, split E_c = 6 and E_t = 8.

name: tri_cycle_k8_control_no_violation
statement: Tri-cycle k=8 (r = 16, |D| = 24 = r + k, excess required 8): the cyclic subspace R = span{e0+e2, e2+e4, e4+e6} of dim 3 gives excess exactly 6 = 2d, NOT 7. The pair-sum upper bound for the object is d_cb <= 4.
notes: This was the decisive registered test - the bound claims d_cb >= 4 at k=8 and therefore needs the lemma at d = 3, exactly where the counterexamples live - and the violation VANISHED. || WHY: at k=4 the hubs are 0,2,4,6 and those three pair-sums CLOSE the hub cycle, since the fourth pair-sum e6+e0 already lies in their span. At k=8 the hub cycle has eight vertices, so three pair-sums close nothing, only three lines lie in R, and excess = 2d exactly. || That is what isolated the cycle-rank mechanism: the violation requires a CLOSED cycle of pair-sums, which is the c in excess = 2d + c. || INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED while filing this store: |D| = 24, d = 3, eighteen classes, excess exactly 6, split E_c = 3 and E_t = 3. This is the negative control for the two counterexamples and it fires the right way - same construction, same dimension, no violation.

name: excess_at_most_2d_refuted
statement: The lemma excess <= 2d, on which the campaign's counting bound d_cb >= ceil(k/2) rested, is FALSE for linear triangle systems. Killing witness: tri-cycle k=4 with R = span{e0+e2, e2+e4, e4+e6}, dimension 3, excess 7.
notes: A second witness at tri-cycle k=6 gives excess 11 at d = 5. || WHAT SURVIVED THE KILL, stated at the time rather than reconstructed later: excess <= 2 at d = 1 is proved and the controls reproduce it; the CONCLUSION d_cb >= ceil(k/2) still holds on every object ever measured (tri-cycles k=3..7 give 2,2,3,3,4 = ceil(k/2) throughout, and no measured object has fallen below the bound); and the counterexamples sit at d = k-1, far above the d = ceil(k/2) - 1 that the counting bound actually uses, so they did not immediately touch k <= 6. What died is the derivation, not the conclusion.

name: excess_at_most_2d_plus_one_refuted
statement: The repaired bound excess <= 2d+1 - proposed after excess <= 2d fell, with the +1 attributed to a single closed pair-sum cycle - is FALSE as well. Killing witness: two coordinate-disjoint tri-cycle k=4 blocks (k = 8), dimension 6, excess 14 against 2d+1 = 13.
notes: The repair lasted one experiment, and the experiment was chosen to break it rather than to confirm it. Under excess <= 2d+1 the counting bound survived for EVEN k only (2d+1 >= k gives d >= k/2 for even k, but only (k-1)/2 for odd k); with the +1 replaced by the cycle rank c, the counting bound is unsupported at EVERY k.

name: E_t_at_most_d_refuted
statement: E_t <= d - the single unproved link the counting-bound derivation had been reduced to, and the campaign's declared open lemma - is FALSE. It follows from two facts already on record: excess = E_c + E_t with E_c <= d PROVED, and the tri-cycle k=4 witness with excess 7 at d = 3. Then E_t = 7 - E_c >= 7 - 3 = 4 > 3 = d.
notes: PROVENANCE, stated because it matters: the deduction was drawn while filing this store, from two results the campaign already holds, and was then CHECKED by direct recomputation on an independent reimplementation of the merge/class machinery written from the definitions - which reproduced |D| = 12, d = 3, five classes, the class-size vector [4,2,2,2,2] and excess 7 exactly as reported, and split them as E_c = 3, E_t = 4. Two further witnesses give the same verdict: tri-cycle k=6 has E_c = 5 and E_t = 6 at d = 5, and two tri-cycle k=4 blocks have E_c = 6 and E_t = 8 at d = 6. Both controls of the same pass behave (one pair-sum: E_c = E_t = 1 at d = 1; two disjoint pair-sums: E_c = E_t = 2 at d = 2), so the detector is alive in both directions. || CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD: the campaign's standing list of open items should no longer carry 'E_t <= d' as open. It is settled, in the negative, and the honest reading of the counting bound is that it now has no derivation at all rather than one missing lemma. This is a correction TO the campaign's own status list, not a transcription of it.

name: counting_bound_derivation_invalidated
statement: The derivation d_cb >= ceil(k/2) FROM excess <= 2d is invalid. Both the original bound and its repair are refuted, so the counting bound is now a conjecture supported by measurement rather than a bound with an argument behind it.
notes: WHAT IS AND IS NOT KILLED. Killed: the inference chain |D| = r+k, excess needed = k, excess <= 2d, therefore d >= ceil(k/2). Not killed: the conclusion, which holds on every object the campaign has ever measured; |D| = r + k, which is independent of this; excess <= 2 at d = 1, which is proved; and the star and disjoint theorems, which never used this argument. || The lower bound max(ceil(k/2), k-h) inherits the same status - its ceil(k/2) term loses its derivation, and its k-h term rests on the same per-dimension counting.

name: how_far_dense_linear_systems_erode_the_counting_bound
statement: RESOLVED 2026-08-20, in the direction feared. The erosion is real and UNBOUNDED: for K_{q,q} in the bipartite hub construction, d_cb <= 2q-1 = 2*sqrt(k)-1 while ceil(k/2) = Theta(k), ratio 1.00, 0.69, 0.52, 0.42, 0.34 for q = 3,5,7,9,11, tending to zero. So the counting argument gives at best something of order sqrt(k), exactly as the estimate suggested, and d_cb >= ceil(k/2) is false for linear systems.
notes: THE TEST NAMED IN THIS OBJECT WAS RUN AND IT SETTLED IT. The self-limiting guess - that density and 2-colourability pull against each other - is WRONG, and the reason is worth keeping: the construction puts the density in the CHOSEN PAIR-GRAPH while fresh hub points keep the TRIPLE SYSTEM sparse and 2-colourable. K_{5,5} has k/r = 1.67, deep in the regime sec.24 measured as empty, yet |A| = 186 and the fibre spans. sec.24's 'structurally obstructed' verdict was drawn from RANDOM maximal partial Steiner systems and does not survive a structured construction.

name: fano_plane_empty_fibre
statement: The Fano plane - 7 triples on 7 points, every pair in exactly one triple, any two triples meeting in exactly one point, the densest linear system on 7 points, whose pair graph is the complete graph K7 so that all 21 pairs are merge-carrying - has |A| = 0. It admits no valid sign vector at all, so d_cb is not defined on it.
notes: This is the classical fact that the Fano plane is not 2-colourable (hypergraph chromatic number 3): every +-1 assignment leaves some line monochromatic, so the fibre is empty. Measured here rather than quoted, and it agrees with the classical statement. || WHY IT MATTERS: the densest linear system cannot be used against the counting bound, because the bound is a statement about d_cb and d_cb needs a non-empty fibre. So the densest linear systems have EMPTY fibres, which may be exactly what protects the counting bound. || WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not un-refute excess <= 2d or excess <= 2d+1, which died on tri-cycles with perfectly good non-empty fibres; it does not restore the counting bound's derivation; and it says nothing about partial Steiner systems sparser than Fano, which may have both density and 2-colourability. It removes one specific route by which the damage looked unbounded, no more.

name: linked_pair_characterisation_of_dcb
statement: For a linear triangle system, d_cb is the least d such that d LINKED pairs (1_{S_j}, e_t), with j in t, span Q^k. Here S_j is the set of triangles containing coordinate j, e_t is the unit vector of triangle t in the relation-coefficient space Q^k, and the pair is LINKED because a pair-sum v = e_y + e_z of triangle t = (x,y,z) merges f_t with e_x and e_y with -e_z, so both constraints it supplies come from the SAME triangle: a hub vector and a unit cannot be drawn from different triangles within one dimension.
notes: MATCHES 34 OF 34 OBJECTS, no misses, spanning stars, chains, paths, fans, wheels, tri-cycles, disjoint unions, mixed shapes, and every attachment profile at k = 6. Five predictions were computed from the model and then measured by an independent pair-sum search: (2,2,2) k=7 -> 4, (3,2,1) k=7 -> 4, (4,1,1) k=7 -> 5, star4 + pendant chain3 -> 4, tri-cycle k=6 -> 3. Five for five. || WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE THREE FORMULAS IT REPLACES. It makes the discrimination no (k,h) formula can: (3,1,1) and (2,2,1) have the same k = 6 and the same h = 3 and come in at 4 and 3, so any expression in k and h alone is wrong about one of them - which is exactly how the connected conjecture died. It REPRODUCES the two proved theorems rather than being fitted to them (star k-1, disjoint m). And it is a restatement of the blocking theorem, which is PROVED, rather than a new hypothesis: blocking says a transversal is independent exactly when the missed set's constraints have rank k, and this says d_cb is the least number of dimensions whose linked constraints reach that rank. || WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. It is verified, not proved. The lower direction needs that a dimension supplies at most two constraints of this form, which rested on E_t <= d - now REFUTED, so that half is worse off than when the characterisation was written. The upper direction needs that a spanning selection can always be realised as an actual subspace, which is verified and not argued. Being a characterisation rather than a formula, it computes d_cb rather than predicting it from parameters, which makes it less falsifiable per object and more useful as a bridge. || SCOPE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: it fails off linear systems, always by overestimating - see linked_pair_overestimates_off_linear_systems.

name: linked_pair_overestimates_off_linear_systems
statement: The linked-pair characterisation FAILS on non-linear systems, on 5 of the 7 tested, and the direction is uniform - it OVERESTIMATES. Linked-pair value against exact d_cb: wheel k=4 2 vs 2 (agrees), fan k=4 2 vs 2 (agrees), wheel k=5 3 vs 2, wheel k=6 3 vs 2, book p=3 2 vs 1, book p=4 3 vs 1, fan k=5 3 vs 2.
notes: THIS IS THE SIGN THE MECHANISM REQUIRES, which is why it is filed as evidence FOR the characterisation's account of itself rather than against it: a non-linear system lets one vector retire more than two forms, so fewer dimensions suffice than the linked-pair count allows. The two agreements are the small cases where the extra merging power has nothing to buy. || The scope boundary was registered before the run - the derivation needs excess <= 2d, which book p=3 already breaks, so off linear systems the characterisation has no right to work, and if it had worked anyway the account of WHY it works would be wrong.

name: dcb_exact_3_1_1_at_k6_is_4
statement: For the triangle-tree with attachment profile (3,1,1) at k=6 - triangles T0=(0,1,2), T1=(0,3,4), T2=(0,5,6), T3=(0,7,8), T4=(1,9,10), T5=(2,11,12), r = 13, hubs 0,1,2 so h = 3 - d_cb = 4 exactly.
notes: THREE ROUTES, TWO OF THEM INDEPENDENT. (1) By hand from the linked-pair structure: 1_{S_0} = (1,1,1,1,0,0) treats T1,T2,T3 symmetrically and no other available vector distinguishes them, so separating three triangles needs at least TWO of the units e_1,e_2,e_3, each costing a dimension spent at that triangle; that leaves one dimension to produce both 1_{S_1} = (1,0,0,0,1,0) and 1_{S_2} = (1,0,0,0,0,1), and no single dimension does, since T0 yields 1_{S_0} together with only ONE of them and a dimension at T4 or T5 yields only its own hub. (2) Linked-pair spanning number: 4. (3) EXHAUSTIVE fast_dcb over every line, dmax = 4, returning exactly 4 in 5289s, with a separate d <= 3 exhaustion (2962s) confirming > 3 from the other direction. || Routes 1 and 2 share an underlying picture and are NOT independent of each other; route 3 shares nothing with either, which is what makes this the campaign's strongest single value. || A FIRST VERSION OF THE HAND ARGUMENT reached the right answer while omitting a case - a triangle whose three coordinates are all hubs can supply two hub vectors and no unit, so T0 can contribute (1_{S_0}, 1_{S_1}) or (1_{S_0}, 1_{S_2}). The conclusion survives by the cleaner route above. Recorded because an argument that happens to be right is not the same as one that has considered its alternatives.

name: dcb_exact_4_1_at_k6_is_4
statement: For the triangle-tree with attachment profile (4,1) at k=6, d_cb = 4 exactly.
notes: Exhaustive fast_dcb, dmax = 4, returning exactly 4 in 5851s, cross-checked against a separate d <= 3 exhaustion (3423s) that returned > 3. Two search directions, same answer. Together with (3,1,1) this closes the two profiles left bracketed [3,4] by the k=6 squeeze, so the k=6 tree sweep is now complete: star 5, (4,1) 4, (3,2) 4, (3,1,1) 4, (2,2,1) 3, (2,1,1,1) 3, (1,1,1,1,1) 3, chain 3.

name: dcb_k7_pairsum_upper_bounds
statement: Pair-sum upper bounds at k = 7, each with an explicit witness subspace: star 6 (also k-1 by the star theorem), (5,1) 5, (4,2) 5, (3,3) 5, (4,1,1) 5, (3,2,1) 4, (2,2,2) 4, chain 4, tri-cycle 4, star4 + pendant chain3 4.
notes: THESE CERTIFY d_cb <= value, not equality: the pair-sum search is incomplete once 2d exceeds k, so a hit is an upper bound and a miss proves nothing. Soundness is never at risk, only tightness. The same search recovered all eleven known exact d_cb values in control runs, and the star k=7 row agrees with a proved theorem, so a missing lower witness is strong evidence rather than silence - but it is evidence. || (4,2) and (3,3) were the registered discriminating cases between the dead max(largest group, ceil(k/2)) formula (which said 4) and the hub-count formula (which said 5). Both came in at 5, with star k=6 and (3,2) k=6 passing as in-run controls. The hub formula won that test and was refuted an hour later on a different object, which is worth keeping visible: winning a discriminating test is not survival. || THE CHECK THIS EVIDENCE CANNOT SUPPLY: a full fast_dcb search over every line on one k=7 shape where only the pair-sum search has spoken. Expensive at r = 15, and it is the honest next test of the shared half of the 34.

name: sweep_support_and_discriminating_row_accounting
statement: Two reusable accounting rules, both paid for in this session. (1) A random sweep is only as good as its GENERATOR'S SUPPORT: 32 random linear systems confirmed the global hub formula and were structurally blind to its failure, because every generator written produced CONNECTED systems and the failure was about disconnection. Before trusting a sweep, ask what inputs it cannot produce. (2) Count DISCRIMINATING rows, not rows: when the sweep was rerun with a disconnection-capable generator, 24 systems produced only 2 that separated the two candidate formulas - so 'tested on 24 systems' would have overstated the evidence twelvefold.
notes: APPLIED TO THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN HEADLINE COUNT. The linked-pair characterisation's 34 of 34 was split by how each value was obtained rather than reported as 34 independent confirmations: about 21 could have diverged from the model and did not (the star theorem at k = 2..7, the disjoint theorem at m = 1,2,3, full fast_dcb searches over every line on chain k=2,4,5, path k=3, (2,1) and (1,1,1) at k=4, (3,1),(2,2),(2,1,1) at k=5, tri-cycles k=3,4,5, and the two exhaustive k=6 runs); 5 are partly shared (the k=6 sweep rows, whose lower half is an exhaustive search over all lines and whose upper half is a pair-sum witness); and the rest are fully shared, confirming that the model is self-consistent rather than that it is right. || A THIRD RULE, from the same day: a fitted pattern dies on the prediction you REGISTER, not on the enumeration you extend. Nine straight predictive hits did not save the max(largest group, ceil(k/2)) formula; the tenth killed it.

name: dcb_at_most_k_construction
statement: For every linear triangle system, d_cb <= k, by a construction with no search. A dimension drawn from triangle t can always supply the unit e_t - by missing f_t rather than a coordinate, which needs no hub and no non-hub coordinate. Taking one pair-sum per triangle therefore yields all k units, and those span Q^k.
notes: CHECKED AS A CONSTRUCTION, not inferred: on 13 handpicked objects the k chosen pair-sums are linearly independent AND satisfy valid_R, so the bound comes with an explicit witness; on 22 randomly generated linear systems from a generator that emits both connected and disconnected ones, the NATURAL choice - each triangle contributes the pair of its two later coordinates - was independent and valid_R on 22 of 22, and the greedy fallback was never needed. 35 in total. || CONDITIONAL ON WHAT, precisely: a general proof needs one pair per triangle whose unsigned incidence vectors e_y + e_z are independent over Q, which holds exactly when every component of the graph they form has at most one cycle and that cycle is odd. A choice forming a forest therefore always works, and on a TREE the natural choice is a forest for free, since each triangle's two new coordinates appear in no other chosen pair. For an arbitrary linear system one needs a choice satisfying that no-even-cycle condition; it held in every case checked and the natural choice never failed, but 'the natural choice always works' is not argued. || PARTLY CLOSED 2026-08-20 (sec.39): the independence requirement is a transversal problem, so RADO applies - an independent one-pair-per-triangle choice exists iff every subfamily of s triangles touches >= s coordinates. The rank of a union of triangles IS the number of coordinates touched (each component carries a 3-cycle so none is bipartite; 220 subfamilies, zero mismatches). Linearity forces that for s <= 8 (3s <= C(V',2) with V' <= s-1 needs s >= 9), so d_cb <= k is PROVED for k <= 8. The Hall condition is exactly right and does fail - K_{3,4}, K_{4,4} - where the bound survives via d_cb <= r or additivity instead.

name: conjecture_RC_for_trees_and_disjoint_unions
statement: Conjecture RC - tightness d_cb * beta / ell <= 1, beta = log2(4/3) - holds for the ENTIRE triangle-tree family and for all disjoint unions of triples, as families rather than as enumerated members. A triangle-tree has r = 2k+1 and |A| = 6*3^(k-1), so ell = k*beta exactly and ell/beta = k; a disjoint union of m triples has r = 3m and |A| = 6^m, so ell = m*beta. With d_cb <= k this gives tightness = d_cb/k <= 1 in both cases.
notes: CONDITIONAL on d_cb <= k, which is a verified construction rather than a theorem. Measured ell/beta came out at exactly 3.000, 4.000, 5.000, 6.000 on the trees, as the identity requires. || RC NOW HOLDS ON THREE FAMILIES FOR TWO DIFFERENT REASONS. The dossier's tag 38d proves d <= ell(A_n)/log2(4/3) for the rooted NAE cycle family, which is d_cb <= ell/beta, exactly this campaign's tightness <= 1. What is added here is the other side: d_cb <= k with ell = k*beta gives the same bound for triangle-trees and disjoint unions. || Nothing here touches the sharp Rademacher conjecture - RC is a statement about finite sign fibres that are known NON-MEMBERS of the residual class the conjecture's proof route concerns.

name: rc_does_not_close_on_tri_cycles
statement: OPEN: the d_cb <= k route does NOT close Conjecture RC for cyclic linear systems, because ell = k*beta fails there. Measured ell/beta: trees k=3..6 exactly k (bound on tightness 1.0000); disjoint m=3 3.000 (1.0000); tri-cycle k=3 3.131 (0.9581); tri-cycle k=4 3.957 (bound 1.0108); tri-cycle k=5 5.014 (0.9971). At tri-cycle k=4 the bound k*beta/ell = 1.0108 permits tightness above 1 and therefore proves nothing.
notes: The MEASURED value at tri-cycle k=4 is fine - d_cb = 2 gives tightness 0.5054 - but that is a measurement, not the argument. Closing RC for cycles needs either a better upper bound than d_cb <= k, or the exact ell for cyclic linear systems, which is not k*beta. || This is the sharpest open item the RC line has, and it is a finite computation on a family the campaign can already generate.

name: tightness_normalisation_vs_cycle_ratio_limit
statement: The dossier's cycle_rigidity_ratio_limit d_cb(A_n)/ell(A_n) -> 1/(3(1 - log2 phi)) = 1.090186... and this campaign's tightness d_cb * beta / ell are DIFFERENT normalisations differing by the factor beta = log2(4/3) = 0.4150375. In beta units the cycle limit is 1.0901868 * 0.4150375 = 0.45247, comfortably below 1, so the cycles do not threaten RC.
notes: Recorded because the two numbers invite exactly the wrong comparison. The 'constant-one ceiling' that the cycles EXCEED is the d_cb <= ell statement, which the dossier records as disproved; d_cb <= ell/beta is the surviving one and is what this campaign calls RC. Confusing them would read a proved dossier result as a refutation of the campaign's conjecture.

name: wheel_is_rooted_nae_cycle_and_fan_is_rooted_nae_path
statement: The dossier's rooted NAE cycle A_n = {(a, b_1..b_n) : a + b_i + b_{i+1} in {+-1}, indices cyclic} is precisely this campaign's WHEEL: the triples (0, i, i+1) around a cycle, all sharing coordinate 0. The dossier's rooted NAE PATH on N vertices is precisely this campaign's FAN: the same triples taken non-cyclically, so a fan of k triangles has N = k+1 rim vertices and N-1 = k triples.
notes: An identification by unfolding definitions, not a computation. It is the first bridge between the campaign's own objects and the document's proved theorems, and it turns two of the campaign's most awkward counterexamples into the document's solved cases. || Consequently the dossier's tag 35, d_cb(A_n) = d_geo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) for n >= 4, is a statement about wheels, and tag 38f, d_cb = d_geo = ceil((N-1)/3) for the path, is a statement about fans, predicting ceil(k/3) for a fan of k triangles.

name: ten_agreements_with_the_dossiers_proved_values
statement: Ten values measured independently by this campaign's exact search, with no knowledge of the theorems, agree with two separately proved dossier results. UNROOTED wheels against tag 35's ceil(n/3): n=3 -> 1, n=4 -> 2, n=5 -> 2, n=6 -> 2. UNROOTED fans against tag 38f's ceil(k/3): k=3 -> 1, k=4 -> 2, k=5 -> 2. ROOTED fans against tag 38g's ceil((m+1)/3) with m = k-1, windows W = {0,1,k+1}: k=3 -> 1, k=4 -> 2, k=5 -> 2.
notes: NEITHER FAMILY WAS CHOSEN WITH THOSE THEOREMS IN VIEW: both were built as NON-LINEAR CONTROLS for the counting bound, and their disagreement with that bound is what made them interesting here. The agreement was noticed afterwards. That is what makes this an external validation of the campaign's exact-d_cb machinery rather than a self-check. || The n=3 wheel row sits outside the theorem's stated range (the dossier states tag 35 for n >= 4, the 3-cycle being a known degenerate case where the rim closes on itself immediately), so it is a match against the formula rather than against the theorem. || Wheel n=4 and n=5 were later re-measured over the FULL line set rather than pair-sums alone and agreed again; those are re-measurements of two of the ten, not two further agreements.

name: wheel_counting_bound_gap_is_the_solved_case
statement: The counting bound's violation on wheels is exactly the gap between ceil(n/2) and ceil(n/3). A wheel has r = n+1 and |D| = 2n+1, so |D| - r = n and the counting bound would demand ceil(n/2), while the dossier's proved value is ceil(n/3). That accounts quantitatively for the measured violations at wheels k=3,5,6.
notes: THE READING THIS SUPPORTS: the families that violate the campaign's counting bound are exactly the families the document has already solved, and the boundary between settled and open runs along LINEARITY from both directions - the document solves the non-linear families, the campaign's machinery covers the linear ones, and each breaks where the other works. || The mechanism is the one identified independently here: a wheel is non-linear because consecutive triples share the edge {0, i+1}. || A CORRECTION carried with this object: |D| = r + k is NOT a linearity phenomenon. It holds on every object measured except wheel k=3 - linear or not - so non-linearity does not produce extra dual forms. The counting bound's failure off linear systems is purely a failure of excess <= 2d. Book p=3 remains the clean witness, with |D| = 8 = r + k exactly as everywhere else.

name: rooted_target_is_deletion_independence
statement: In the pair-sum frame the dossier's connector clause becomes combinatorial. A combination of chosen pair-sums lies in span W exactly when it vanishes at every coordinate OUTSIDE W. Hence R int span W = 0 if and only if the chosen vectors, restricted to the non-W coordinates, are still linearly independent. The rooted target therefore asks for pair-sums that both BLOCK (their constraints span Q^k, per the blocking theorem) and SURVIVE DELETION of the window.
notes: This is the campaign's opening of the NAMED GAP - the dossier's open statement is the ROOTED selector distance, a subspace meeting the selector condition AND satisfying R int span W subset R_<, which with R_< = 0 is R int span W = 0. Everything the campaign had measured before this was the UNROOTED distance. || It is elementary linear algebra, and its value is that it makes the rooted condition computable by the same machinery as the unrooted one, which is what produced the rooted fan agreements and the two raising windows.

name: rooted_dimension_ceiling_r_minus_w
statement: After deleting the window, only r - |W| coordinates remain and the chosen vectors must stay independent there, so rooted d <= r - |W|. When no valid R survives the deletion the window BLOCKS outright.
notes: A counting obstruction rather than a structural one, and it explains part of the blocking profile: fan k=4 blocks at |W| = 5 with r = 6 purely by arithmetic (r - w = 1 < 2), whereas fan k=3's blocks at |W| = 4 with r = 5 cap d at 1 and then find no valid one-dimensional R. Distinguishing arithmetic blocks from structural ones matters: only the structural ones are evidence about the connector condition.

name: rooted_fan_matches_dossier_path_theorem
statement: Rooted minima computed from the deletion-independence reading, with W = {0, 1, k+1}: fan k=3 gives 1, fan k=4 gives 2, fan k=5 gives 2. The dossier's tag 38g gives d_m = ceil((m+1)/3) with m = N-2 = k-1 interior private vertices, i.e. ceil(k/3) - 1, 2, 2. Three for three.
notes: Computed with no knowledge of the construction the dossier uses, on the one object where the campaign and the document state the same rooted question. This is the first evidence the campaign has on what the named gap actually asks, as opposed to its unrooted shadow.

name: two_raising_windows
statement: Across roughly five thousand windows enumerated exhaustively by size, EXACTLY TWO raise the rooted dimension above the unrooted one, and each is unique at its size. (1) Fan k=3, window {0,2,3}: rooted 2 against unrooted 1. That window is exactly the middle triangle (0,2,3). (2) Chain k=6 (r = 13), window {4,5,6,7,8}: rooted 4 against unrooted 3, one window in 1,287. That window is exactly the two adjacent triangles (4,5,6) and (6,7,8).
notes: BOTH ARE UNIONS OF WHOLE TRIANGLES, and covering a triangle entirely removes every pair-sum it could contribute, since all three of its pairs then lie inside span W. THAT IS AN OBSERVATION, NOT A MECHANISM, and here is the case that stops it being one: chain k=4's window {0,1,2} also covers a whole triangle and does NOT raise the dimension, nor do the whole-triangle windows of chain k=5. Covering triangles is necessary-looking and plainly not sufficient, and what distinguishes chain k=6's pair from chain k=4's and k=5's is NOT established. || The obvious next guess - that the surviving triangles must still contain an independent set of size ceil(k/2) - is already known to be the wrong shape, because the selection criterion for a valid R is constraint RANK, not independence of the chosen triangles, and independence was shown to be fatal rather than sufficient on (2,1,1,1) at k=6. Recorded as considered and rejected on existing evidence. || NO FOURTH MECHANISM IS BEING OFFERED. Three guesses died in this line already, each by generalising from the smallest object.

name: blocking_windows_verified_on_full_line_set
statement: The blocking and raising results are not an artefact of searching pair-sums only. Re-run over EVERY line of the dual: fan k=3 windows {0,1,2,3} and {0,2,3,4} find nothing under either search (genuinely blocked); fan k=3 window {0,2,3} gives 2 under both (the raise is real); and five controls agree between the two searches - fan k=3 {1,4} gives 1, star k=3 {1,2,3,4,5} gives 2, star k=3 {0} gives 2, chain k=4 {0,1,2} gives 2.
notes: The caveat this answers was registered when the sweep was reported: a 'block' had meant that no PAIR-SUM R survives the window rather than that no R whatsoever does, and the argument that non-pair-sum directions have excess 1 and cannot help reach a maximal-excess subspace was an argument rather than a check. It has now been checked on these seven windows. It does NOT extend the check to every blocking window in the profile.

name: tri_cycles_never_block_refuted
statement: The reading 'tri-cycles never block' is FALSE and was a window-size artefact. Extending tri-cycle k=6 (r = 12) past the earlier sweep's |W| <= 5: at |W| = 3,4,5,6 there are 0 blocks (220, 495, 792, 924 windows), and at |W| = 7 there are 6 blocks in 792 windows. Since r - |W| = 5 still exceeds the unrooted value 3, these are STRUCTURAL blocks, not the arithmetic ceiling.
notes: The earlier reading - that cyclic structure is MORE robust to rooting than tree-like structure, cutting against the intuition that cyclic blocks are the hard case - was an artefact of stopping at |W| = 5. That is the failure mode this campaign has hit repeatedly: a maximum over a bounded enumeration read as a property of the objects. The claim had been flagged as 'worth checking on bigger cycles before being believed' when it was made, and the check killed it.

name: rooting_is_free_or_fatal_refuted
statement: The reading 'rooting is free or fatal, almost never merely expensive' is FALSE. Killing witness: chain k=6 (r = 13) at |W| = 5 has worst rooted 4 against an unrooted 3 - one window in 1,287, alongside 2 blocks. So dimension-raising is not confined to the single small object that produced the reading.
notes: The honest form that replaces it: RAISES ARE RARE - two known across roughly five thousand windows - BUT THEY OCCUR ON LARGE OBJECTS AS WELL AS SMALL. Rarity is not confinement, and the previous statement conflated them. || WHAT THE DEAD READING WAS BEING USED FOR, so the loss is visible: if the rooted dimension equalled the unrooted one wherever it is defined, the rooted constant would be the unrooted constant and the whole difficulty of the named gap would sit in FEASIBILITY - which windows admit a valid R at all - rather than in a worse bound. That reframing is no longer supported, though the raises remain rare enough that the question of how much worse is open.

name: raising_window_is_the_hub_set_refuted
statement: The mechanism 'the raising window is the hub set' is FALSE. It is true for fan k=3, where the hub set {0,2,3} is the unique raising window, and false everywhere else tested: chain k=4's hub set {2,4,6} gives 2 (free), chain k=5's {2,4,6,8} gives 3 (free), and chain k=6's {2,4,6,8,10} gives 3 (free) even though chain k=6 DOES have a raising window at exactly that size.
notes: So the size coincidence at chain k=6 - hubs {2,4,6,8,10}, raise at |W| = 5 - is a coincidence, and whatever raises the dimension there is a different window, namely {4,5,6,7,8}. || The guess had a plausible story behind it: fan k=3's construction wants e_2 + e_3 from the middle triangle (0,2,3) and both of those coordinates are hubs, so once W contains {0,2,3} that vector lies in span W and is forbidden. The story is right about fan k=3 and does not generalise. What the fan k=3 case actually shows is narrower: the cost of rooting is not about the window containing hubs as such, but about the window containing BOTH COORDINATES OF A PAIR-SUM THE CONSTRUCTION NEEDS. The star never suffers this, because its useful pair-sums are arm pairs built from two PRIVATE coordinates, which survive any window containing only the hub.

name: no_wheel_window_has_raised_the_dimension
statement: On the named gap's own family, no window has raised the rooted dimension in any sweep run. Wheel n=4: 0 raises at |W| <= 3, 5 blocks at |W| = 4, unrooted 2 matching the dossier's ceil(n/3) = 2. Wheel n=5: 0 raises at |W| <= 4, 0 blocks so far, unrooted 2 matching ceil(n/3) = 2.
notes: STATED AS THE BOUND OF A SWEEP, NOT AS A PROPERTY OF WHEELS, because that exact conflation has now failed twice in this line - 'tri-cycles never block' and 'rooting is free or fatal' both died on extending the window size. The two known raising windows are both on tree-like objects, and the wheel sweep has not reached the window sizes at which tri-cycle k=6 first blocked. || It matters which family this is: wheels are the rooted NAE cycles, the family the dossier has solved exactly, so 'rooting is so far free on wheels' is a statement about the solved case.

name: max_two_largest_group_formula_refuted
statement: The formula d_cb = max(2, largest attachment group) for triangle-trees at k >= 3 is FALSE. Killing witness: the chain at k=5, whose profile is (1,1,1,1) with largest group 1, so the formula says 2 while the measured value is 3.
notes: The first of five formulas of mine to die in this session. It had fitted seven values across three k, and it was published about an hour before the chain k=5 run that killed it. It also carried a stated exception rather than a smoothed one - star k=2 has d_cb = 1 while max(2,1) = 2 - which is why it was labelled a fitted pattern at the time. || Its successor, max(largest attachment group, ceil(k/2)), is recorded separately as largest_group_formula_refuted and was killed by (3,2) at k=6.

name: global_hub_count_formula_refuted
statement: The formula d_cb = max(ceil(k/2), k - h), applied GLOBALLY to an arbitrary linear triangle system, is FALSE. Killing witness: chain3 disjoint-union chain3 (r = 14), read as one system with k = 6 and h = 4, giving max(3,2) = 3, while the true value is 4.
notes: THE REFUTATION DOES NOT REST ON A MEASUREMENT: additivity is proved and chain k=3 is exact at 2, so 4 is forced. The computation only confirms it. || NOR IS IT A ONE-OFF: ceil(a/2) + ceil(b/2) > ceil((a+b)/2) whenever a and b are both odd, so EVERY pair of odd-length chains breaks it, and chain3 + chain3 is simply the smallest. || WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: writing max(ceil(k/2), k-h) for an arbitrary system silently asserted that the formula commutes with disjoint union, which additivity forbids. That was an unstated assumption, not a discovery about d_cb, and the correction - apply it per connected component and sum - adds no new content, since it is just proved additivity plus the connected case. The connected case then died on its own (see connected_hub_count_formula_refuted). || The LOWER bound max(ceil(k/2), k-h) <= d_cb survived this particular refutation unchanged; only the equality died here.

name: connected_hub_count_formula_refuted
statement: The surviving CONNECTED form of the conjecture - for a connected linear triangle system, d_cb = max(ceil(k/2), k - h) - is FALSE. Killing witness: (3,1,1) at k=6, where h = 3 so the formula gives max(3,3) = 3, and d_cb = 4.
notes: PROVED BY HAND before the machine returned, and then confirmed by an exhaustive fast_dcb search (5289s) that shares nothing with the hand argument. The refutation was also REGISTERED IN ADVANCE, with the expectation stated that my own formula would lose. || WHY h CANNOT BE THE INVARIANT: (2,2,1) has the same k = 6 and the same h = 3 and comes in at 3. There hub 0 covers only three triangles, so 1_{S_0} - e_0 - e_1 = e_2 separates and rank 6 is reached at d = 3. The difference is the SIZE of the largest hub relative to the units its triangles can supply: (3,1,1) has a hub covering four triangles while only three of them can contribute a unit and only one dimension can be spent there without wasting a repeat. || The formula is still correct on all four k=7 connected shapes tested (star 6, tri-cycle 4, chain 4, star4+pendant chain3 4). That is not a rehabilitation - a formula can be right on many objects and still be false - but it locates the failure: it breaks on objects where a hub covers more triangles than the units its own triangles can supply, and not on the shapes where the floor binds.

name: dcb_additivity_over_disjoint_blocks
statement: d_cb adds over coordinate-disjoint blocks: for a linear triangle system S with connected components C, d_cb(S) = sum over C of d_cb(C).
notes: PROVENANCE: this is the campaign's proved additivity lemma, recorded as proved in STATE.md's 20:4x block; the four documents this store layer was extracted from USE it rather than re-deriving it, and its proof is not reproduced there. The disjoint-triples theorem d_cb = m for m disjoint triples is its instance. || It is the instrument that killed the global hub formula without any measurement being needed, and it is what forced the prediction that two disjoint excess-7 blocks give excess 14.

name: chain3_disjoint_chain3_certificate
statement: chain3 disjoint-union chain3 (r = 14) has d_cb = 4, with chain3 alone at 2 and star3 disjoint-union star3 at 4 as in-run controls. Six discriminating multi-component observations in total, all going to the component-wise reading and none against: chain3 + chain3 4 (global says 3), chain3 + triangle 3 (global 2), chain3 + star3 4 (global 3), chain5 + triangle 4 (global 3), and two random 2-component systems at 3 each (global 2).
notes: THE DIRECTION MATTERS AND IS FAVOURABLE: on every row the component-wise value is the LARGER candidate, and a pair-sum search is an UPPER bound, so incompleteness can only push a measurement up. The search could not have manufactured the component answer by being incomplete, and landing on the smaller global value would have refuted the component reading outright. || Two of the six come from a random sweep and four were constructed deliberately, using odd chains and lone triangles as the lever - random generation being a poor way to collect discriminating cases, as 22 of 24 random systems gave the same answer under both readings.

name: independent_triangle_selection_rule_refuted
statement: The construction rule 'choose an independent set of ceil(k/2) triangles in the share-a-coordinate graph' is FALSE. Enumerating every pair-sum subspace of the target dimension and splitting by validity: on chain k=5, 27 of 252 VALID choices are independent and 0 of 203 invalid ones are; on (1,1,1,1,1) at k=6, 135 of 216 valid and 0 of 600 invalid; but on (2,1,1,1) at k=6, ZERO of 108 valid choices are independent while all 135 independent choices sit among the 708 invalid ones. Independence is sufficient on two objects and FATAL on the third.
notes: WHAT ACTUALLY SEPARATES THEM, worked by hand. Take (2,1,1,1)'s independent set {3,4,5} with T3=(1,7,8), T4=(2,9,10), T5=(3,11,12). Their pair-sums give, via hub coordinates 1, 2 and 3, the constraints c_0+c_3=0, c_3=0, c_0+c_4=0, c_4=0, c_1+c_5=0, c_5=0, forcing c_0,c_1,c_3,c_4,c_5 to vanish - rank 5, and c_2 is NEVER TOUCHED, because triangle 2 hangs off hub 0 which none of the chosen pair-sums reaches. The working choice {0,1,3} does reach hub 0, whose constraint c_0+c_1+c_2 = 0 brings c_2 in. On the chain, alternating triangles {0,2,4} reach rank 5 because consecutive hub constraints OVERLAP; independence gives coverage there by accident of the chain's shape. || The rule had scored 13 of 14 across five families with its one structural exception (tri-cycle k=5, where a cycle of k triangles has maximum independent set floor(k/2) < ceil(k/2) so the construction must reuse a triangle) PREDICTED IN ADVANCE. A 13-of-14 score on a proxy is not evidence for the proxy.

name: construction_is_a_rank_condition_on_chosen_pair_sums
statement: The upper-bound construction, stated in the same terms as the lower bound: choose d pair-sums whose INDUCED CONSTRAINT SYSTEM HAS RANK k. This is not a new rule bolted on - it is what the blocking theorem demanded from the start, and every combinatorial shorthand for it (largest attachment group, spreading the triangles, an independent set of triangles) has now failed on some object.
notes: It makes the two halves match: the lower bound says the achievable rank cannot exceed min(2d, d+h), and the construction says pick any d pair-sums achieving rank k. || WHAT REMAINS: an EXISTENCE statement about the incidence structure of the hubs - that such a choice always exists at the target dimension - not a recipe. Sketches exist for the three extremes and each works for a visibly different reason (star: one all-ones hub vector plus k-1 units; disjoint triples: no hub vectors, so k units are required and each pair-sum supplies one; chain: the hub vectors are path incidence vectors of rank k-1, an interior triangle carries two hub coordinates so one pair-sum yields two of them, and an end triangle's non-hub coordinate supplies the missing unit). Three different reasons is usually the sign that the general argument is about the rank of the hub vectors 1_{S_j} together with the units available on triangles carrying a non-hub coordinate.

name: mechanism_guesses_tested_where_they_predict_nothing
statement: A cheap check that killed three mechanism guesses in one line of work: evaluate a proposed mechanism on the objects where it predicts NOTHING should happen, not only on the ones where something did. The three that died - 'the raising window is the hub set', 'rooting is free or fatal', 'tri-cycles never block' - each generalised from the smallest object on which the phenomenon appears, which is exactly where a phenomenon is most likely to be degenerate.
notes: The same shape appears in the excess line: excess <= 2d and excess <= 2d+1 were each read off the objects where the bound was tight and each died on a larger object built to break it. || The discipline that follows: when a pattern is proposed, name in the same breath the object on which it forbids something, and run that one first.

name: search_space_size_is_not_search_cost
statement: An operational scar: fast_dcb returns the FIRST valid subspace it finds, so it pays the full enumeration only when the answer is NOT at that dimension. Two exhaustive runs at k=6 were killed and relaunched on the grounds that a d=4 stage would have to enumerate about C(700,4) ~ 10^10 subspaces at r = 13 and was therefore infeasible. Both would have terminated - and did, when re-run - because the answer was 4 and the search stopped at a witness.
notes: The reasoning confused 'the search space is large' with 'the search must traverse it'. The related sizing error in the other direction, also paid for the same day: a search bound chosen from what one wants to learn rather than from what the search will cost. Both runs completed in under 100 minutes.

name: campaign_objects_are_known_nonmembers_of_the_class
statement: The sharp Rademacher singularity conjecture, Pr(det B_n = 0) = (1+o(1)) * 2 * n^2 * 2^(-n), is OPEN and nothing in this campaign layer bears on it directly. Every object studied here - triangle-trees, tri-cycles, disjoint unions, stars, chains, wheels, fans, books, the Fano plane - is a finite sign fibre that is a KNOWN NON-MEMBER of the dense, singleton-layer cyclic residual class the conjecture's proof route concerns.
notes: Recorded as an object, not only as a banner, so that a query into this store returns it. The campaign's value is in the deterministic Layer-II machinery - selector distance, the blocking reformulation, the rooted deletion condition - and in the counterexamples that constrain any proof. No object here is evidence that the conjecture is true, and this store must never be read or cited as claiming it proved.

name: pasch_forces_four_extra_dual_forms
statement: If a linear triple system contains a Pasch configuration then |D| >= r + k + 4. Labelling the Pasch by its pairwise intersections p_ij, each of the four triples {p_ij, p_il, p_jl} is not-all-equal on the whole fibre and is not a block. Hence |D| = r + k forces the system to be ANTI-PASCH.
notes: PROOF. Suppose s(p12)=s(p13)=s(p23)=eps. B_1={p12,p13,p14} is not-all-equal with two points at eps, so s(p14)=-eps; B_2 gives s(p24)=-eps; B_3 gives s(p34)=-eps; then B_4={p14,p24,p34} is monochromatic, contradiction. Not a block because it contains the pair {p12,p13} already in B_1 and no pair lies in two blocks of a linear system. The four triples are the conjugate Pasch. || Machine-checked on 7 systems: all four conjugate triples +-1 across the whole fibre, none a block, excess 4,4,24,48,72,4,4. || NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT: K_{2,3} and K_{3,3} are anti-Pasch with 6 and 18 extras.

name: bipartite_hub_construction
statement: Given a bipartite graph H, give each edge {x,y} a triple {x,y,z}. Two triples may share a third point when their H-edges are disjoint, so one fresh hub serves a whole matching. Decomposing K_{p,q} into q matchings gives a LINEAR system with k = pq triples on r = p + 2q points whose fibre is never empty (colour H by its bipartition and every triple is not-all-equal whatever the hub does). Choosing the H-edge from every triple makes the chosen pair-graph exactly H, spanning a subspace of dimension |V(H)| - (bipartite components) = p + q - 1.
notes: This is the object that breaks the counting bound and resolves how_far_dense_linear_systems_erode_the_counting_bound. A Pasch rectangle needs two left points with 2(a-a') = 0 mod q, so q ODD gives an anti-Pasch member - predicted and measured on 9 members, both directions. Verified linear by maximum pairwise intersection 1 on the printed triples.

name: counting_bound_statement_refuted_unboundedly
statement: d_cb >= ceil(k/2) is FALSE for linear triangle systems, false for ANTI-PASCH linear systems, and false by an unbounded factor. K_{4,4}: linear, spanning, k=16, r=12, valid R of dimension 7 against ceil(k/2)=8. K_{3,5}, K_{4,5}, K_{5,5}: anti-Pasch and below the bound at 7, 8, 9 against 8, 10, 13. Asymptotically d_cb <= 2*sqrt(k)-1.
notes: Supersedes the weaker counting_bound_derivation_invalidated, which said only that the DERIVATION was gone while the statement held on everything measured. Now the statement is false too. It survives only under the extra hypothesis |D| = r + k, which linearity does not imply. || Validity confirmed by TWO independent implementations - the library's row-reduction test and one that quotients by projection onto a complement of R with its own transversal search - agreeing on every row. || All measurements in secs.1-31 stand.

name: fibre_nonempty_iff_bipartite_pair_choice
statement: For ANY triple system, the fibre is non-empty iff some choice of one pair per triple yields a BIPARTITE pair graph.
notes: Both directions elementary and neither uses linearity. (<=) a bipartite choice's 2-colouring makes every chosen pair bichromatic, so no triple is monochromatic and the colouring read as +-1 IS a valid sign vector. (=>) a valid sign vector gives each triple a bichromatic pair; choosing one per triple yields a graph properly 2-coloured by it. || Verified on 13 hand objects plus 120 random systems including 10 with empty fibres; sharpest case the FANO PLANE, all 3^7 = 2187 choices exhaustively, none bipartite. || Characterises a hypothesis the dossier only ASSUMES: its central object is 'a nonempty antipodal sign fibre, usually assumed spanning', and 2-colourability, Property B, bipartite and monochromatic occur nowhere in its 326KB.

name: no_maximal_partial_steiner_on_8_points_spans
statement: Not one of the 16,200 maximal partial Steiner systems on 8 points has a spanning fibre - complete enumeration, not sampling. 1% empty, 36% too small to span (rank <= |A|/2 since A is antipodal, so |A| < 2r forbids spanning), 62% structurally obstructed, zero usable.
notes: The r=7 control reproduces the sampler's 93% spanning, so the detector finds spanning systems when they exist. || Explained by two windows on k: U(r) = largest k admitting a spanning system, L(r) = smallest k that is maximal. Any spanning system has k <= U and any maximal one k >= L, so L > U forces zero - the implication runs ONE WAY and proves the zeroes while only permitting the positives. U(7)=5=L(7) overlap; U(8)=6 < L(8)=7 disjoint; U(9)=9 (exact, 21,066,170 nodes) with L(9)=8 gives window {8,9}, and the usable systems at r=9 are exactly k in {8,9}. || The structural obstruction is always ONE pair pinned ANTIPODALLY inside a triple: all 407 relations have support 2, codimension is 1 or 3 and never 2, and the codim-3 cases are all one object, s_a=s_b=s_c=-s_x. || CORRECTED SAME NIGHT: r=10 was first recorded as 0 from a 1,200-draw sweep; a wider search over 23,995 systems found 22 spanning ones, each re-verified. Rare, not absent. Only the r=8 zero is a complete enumeration entitled to be read as impossibility.

name: hostile_family_tightness_tends_to_beta
statement: For K_{q,q} in the bipartite hub construction, |A| = 6(2^q - 1) exactly (verified q = 2..13), so ell = 2q - log2(6) + o(1) against d_cb <= 2q-1. Hence d_cb/ell -> 1 and tightness d_cb*beta/ell -> beta = 0.415, from above, falling monotonically 0.575 -> 0.443 over q = 3..13. Conjecture RC is unthreatened by this family at any q.
notes: The objects that destroy the counting bound by an unbounded factor settle at d_cb ~ ell, a factor 1/beta = 2.41 inside RC - mild evidence FOR the conjecture, from the most extreme objects the campaign has built. || The limit being beta itself is suggestive: beta is where the absorption threshold and the minimum congestion cost sit, and a family constructed for an unrelated reason converges to it from the other side. || The closed form for |A| was validated against brute-force enumeration on 6 members before being used beyond brute-force range.

name: dossier_needs_an_upper_bound_not_this_lower_one
statement: The dossier never uses a k/2-style counting step - zero occurrences of k/2, ceil(k/2), 'half the', 'at least k/2' in its 326KB. What it requires is stated outright: 'A bound dcb = O(ell) therefore makes the residual cost commensurate with the entropy loss', against its unconditional dcb <= 9*4^ell + ell. That is an UPPER bound on d_cb; ceil(k/2) is a LOWER bound. Refuting it cannot weaken the programme.
notes: Worth keeping as a methodological point, not only a fact: the campaign spent substantial effort on a quantity facing away from the target. Before mourning a refuted result, check whether the programme ever needed it. || Also: 'Pasch' occurs nowhere in the dossier, although a Pasch is sufficient to wreck the |D| = r+k bookkeeping that the Layer II reconstruction here leaned on.

name: which_linear_systems_have_dual_exactly_r_plus_k
statement: OPEN, and now the honest form of the counting bound's hypothesis: which linear triple systems satisfy |D| = r + k? Anti-Pasch is NECESSARY (proved). It is not sufficient - K_{2,3} and K_{3,3} are anti-Pasch with 6 and 18 extra forms. So the class supporting ceil(k/2) sits strictly inside the anti-Pasch systems and no characterisation is held.
notes: The extras are more varied than implied triples: random linear systems give SIGNED extras (e0-e1+e2, a not-all-equal condition on a triple with one coordinate negated) and larger support (e0+e2+e3+e4+e6, and one form on all seven coordinates). A +-1-valued form of support 5 is a balance condition, not a triple constraint at all. So implied triples are one mechanism, not the mechanism. || Anti-Pasch (quadrilateral-free) systems are a studied family in design theory, so the hypothesis has a name even though the characterisation does not.

name: rado_hall_condition_for_independent_pair_choice
statement: For a linear triangle system, an independent one-pair-per-triangle choice exists IFF every subfamily of s triangles touches at least s coordinates. Proof: it is a transversal problem so Rado applies, and rank(union of s triangles' pair-sums) = V'(S) because every component of a union of triangles carries an odd 3-cycle, so b = 0. Linearity forces the condition for s <= 8 (3s <= C(V',2) with V' <= s-1 requires s >= 9), hence d_cb <= k is proved for every linear system with k <= 8.
notes: Rank identity checked on 220 subfamilies, zero mismatches. The Hall condition predicts the existence of an even-cycle-free choice exactly, 10 of 10 including the two negatives K_{3,4} and K_{4,4}. || Found because a naive greedy FAILED on K_{3,3} while a choice existed: tracing showed it jams on the LAST triangle in the generation order and that 2,272 of 4,000 random orders succeed, so greedy is order-dependent rather than wrong - which is what pointed at matroid transversal instead of sequential construction. || Does NOT prove d_cb <= k in general: where the condition fails the bound may still hold via d_cb <= r or the additivity lemma.
